reason: I'll place Air at the waters to work toward making the heavens.
expectation: I expect air and water to help form the sky or vault, though I'm not sure how.

effect: The air action completed the vault goal and revealed a goal to make dry ground, so I’ll try placing Earth in the Void.
reaction: The result was a little surprising; the step felt worthwhile because it completed a goal and opened the next one.
reason: Earth in the Void seems like a possible way to make dry ground.
expectation: I expect it may create land, though I’m not sure why the Void is the right place.

alternatives.reason: Earth at the waters might also make dry ground, but I’ll try the newly created Void first.

effect: Earth in the Void completed the dry ground goal and revealed a goal to bring light to the earth.
reaction: Making Proto-Earth was straightforward; the step felt worthwhile because it advanced the goal.
reason: Fire seems most likely to provide the light, so I’ll try it at the Void.
expectation: I expect Fire in the Void may create light, though I’m not sure how it will reach the earth.

alternatives.reason: Fire at the waters is another available option, but the Void worked for the previous goal.

effect: Fire in the Void created the Sun, so I can now try it with Proto-Earth to bring light to the earth.
reaction: Creating the Sun made sense; the step felt worthwhile because it supplied something useful for the light goal.
reason: The Sun and Proto-Earth seem like a direct way to bring light to the earth.
expectation: I expect the Sun to light Proto-Earth and possibly complete the light goal.

effect: Combining the Sun and Proto-Earth completed the light goal and revealed a moon goal.
reaction: The result was straightforward; the step felt worthwhile because it completed the light goal.
reason: I'll try Earth at the waters because it is one of the two available combinations, though its connection to the moon is unclear.
expectation: I expect it to create something new, but I don't know whether it will help make the moon.

alternatives.reason: Fire at the waters is also available, but I don't know which is more relevant to the moon.

reaction: The asteroids were unexpected; the step felt mixed because it opened a new option but its connection to the moon is still unclear.
reason: I'll try the new Asteroids with Proto-Earth to see what they make.
expectation: I expect the asteroids and Proto-Earth to create something that may help with the moon, though I'm unsure how.

alternatives.reason: Fire at the waters is also available, but I want to try the newly created Asteroids first.

effect: The asteroid strike created the Moon and revealed a goal to steady the shattered Earth.
reaction: The explanation was surprising; the step felt worthwhile because it connected the asteroids to the Moon and completed a goal.
reason: I'll combine the Moon with Proto-Earth to work toward steadying the Earth.
expectation: I expect the Moon to steady Proto-Earth and possibly complete the new goal.

effect: The Moon and Proto-Earth created a steadied world and completed the goal; Fire at the waters is the remaining combination.
reaction: The gravity explanation was interesting; the step felt worthwhile because it explained how the Moon helps Earth.
reason: I'll use Fire at the waters because it is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect it to create something new, perhaps related to the remaining stars goal, though I'm unsure.

effect: Fire at the waters created Stars and completed the remaining goal, finishing the chapter.
reaction: The result was straightforward; the step felt worthwhile because it completed the chapter, though I didn't understand why the waters made stars.

mostWorthwhile.text: The asteroid strike and Moon explanation were the most worthwhile: they connected the assembly to an unexpected result. Playing through felt worth the effort, though the straightforward assembly was less interesting than that explanation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Creating Stars felt a little weak because the connection between Fire at the waters and stars was unclear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that an asteroid strike created the Moon, and interested to learn that the Moon's gravity helps steady Earth's tilt.

arbitrary.text: Earth at the waters producing Asteroids and Fire at the waters producing Stars both felt somewhat arbitrary from the text, even though the asteroids later had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I'm not sure I'd choose another chapter. The Moon explanation interested me, but much of the play was straightforward and some combinations were hard to connect to their results.
